name: Edward Perry Warren
bio: Boston paper-fortune heir turned expatriate collector of classical antiquities - the great supplier of the Boston Museum of Fine Arts - and 'master of Lewes House' in Lewes, East Sussex, where from 1890 he 'collected art and young men' and tried to forge his secretaries into a 'brotherhood of aesthetes'. Born at Waltham, Massachusetts, 'in the year Lincoln was elected President'; at New College, Oxford, he met John Marshall in 1884 - 'the love of his life' per Sox - whom he wooed by letter for five years and whose forty-year partnership anchored the enterprise. Author of A Tale of Pausanian Love, the privately printed fairy tale The Prince Who Did Not Exist (1900, dedicated to Mary Bliss), and A Defence of Uranian Love, written and rewritten in his garden office at 'Thebes'. Died in London on 28 December 1928 after an abdominal operation, ten months after Marshall; cremated at Golders Green on 1 January 1929; his ashes were placed in the Marshalls' tomb at Bagni di Lucca on 5 April 1929, next to 'his beloved "Puppy"'.
bio_sources: Born: 'Born at Waltham, Massachusetts near Boston in the year Lincoln was elected President (1860)' - Sox (1991) p. 3
Died: 'Ned was dead on 28 December 1928. After an abdominal operation, he entered the Cambridge House Nursing Home at Dorset Square in London where he died.' - Sox p. 129
Cremation 1 Jan 1929, ashes to Bagni di Lucca 5 Apr 1929, 'collected art and young men', 'brotherhood of aesthetes', 'his beloved Puppy': Sox pp. vii-viii
Lewes House lease April 1890 (first seen Oct 1889): Sox p. 44
Works: A Tale of Pausanian Love, Sox pp. 38, 44; The Prince Who Did Not Exist, p. 75; Defence of Uranian Love at 'Thebes', pp. 153-154 (title italicized in Fothergill's letter at p. 154)
bio_note: Sox gives the birth year only as '(1860)' inside the Lincoln's-election phrase; no month or day in pages read. Oxford matriculation 1883 is implied, not stated ('In January 1884, Prichard entered New College only months after Ned Warren's matriculation', p. 169, rendered). (Cumberland Mills paper), p. 3.
